about-003.text: I'm Adjoa, a food systems strategist and communications architect based in Georgia, raised in New York. My work sits at the intersection of narrative, community & strategy: helping organizations say what they mean, build what they promise, and reach the people who need to find them.

about-021.html: Then I came back to where Seulful Pantry started: making food accessible, affordable, and attainable, through farm-to-table education and catering. Since 2021 I've spent a lot of time on urban farms and in community gardens, and in rooms working on food policy. Along the way I took part in the James Beard Foundation's Chefs Boot Camp for Policy and Change, focused on Child Nutrition Reauthorization, and joined the JBF Legacy Network, the Forté Foundation Fellowship, The Lexicon, Seed Consulting Group, and the Vital Voices GROW Fellowship. I earned my MBA at UNC Kenan-Flagler Business School. These days that looks like marketing for food access, community work in the field, and writing, all pointed at the same thing.

about-016.html: In my early years of writing, I took on African liberation, spirituality, psychology, and how access to food and water shapes the mind. I pulled from writers like Dr. Amos Wilson and Dr. Marimba Ani, and that led me here. I saw the need to nurture the mind through the belly, and I decided to dedicate my life to better food systems.

about-019.html: After studying psychology at SUNY College at Old Westbury, I started out at nonprofits like STRONG Youth and AHRC. As a Direct Support Professional at AHRC, I created a plant-based curriculum that helped people with intellectual and developmental disabilities cook healthy meals on their own. I started documenting my recipes and kitchen experiments online, and people kept asking for more. Within a year, that turned into a meal-prep service called Seulful Pantry, and eventually into cooking privately for a few professional athletes.
